title: Cutflow curator: sprint 29 backlog pruning and triage
content:
Summary:
This is the working doc for Sprint 29 backlog pruning for Console & Rollouts. Goal: reduce WIP by ~30% of current backlog candidates, surface 6 high-confidence deliverables for the sprint, and lock a minimal cutlist for experimental runway. This is a pragmatic trim — keep high-impact, low-risk items and park exploratory/large-risk work.

Context:
- Sprint window: 2026-10-07 -> 2026-10-20 (two-week window with feature freeze on 10/16)
- Current intake queue: ~112 console tickets tagged product-console backlog intake
- Pressure drivers: Dedicated rollout support, upcoming enterprise demo (10/21), and Optimize telemetry migration.

Goals for this triage session:
1) Identify 6 sprint commitments (2 small, 3 medium, 1 canary).
2) Produce a cutlist of items to defer to Q4 planning.
3) Produce wireframe/acceptance criteria for each committed item to unblock design/dev pair.
4) Flag 3 risky tickets for synchronous architecture grooming.

Pruning heuristics (apply in order):
- Customer-impact first: prioritize items referenced in at least 2 CS tickets or a named customer ask.
- Cost-of-delay: immediate demo blockers > roadmap improvements > nice-to-have UX polish.
- Cycle time vs. value: prefer <4d tasks with clarity.
- Cross-team dependency: deprioritize anything needing infra changes unless SLA/enterprise-critical.
- Rework/duplicate detection: collapse overlapping tickets across intake owners.

Filtered backlog (selected candidates with short rationale):
- PROD-4382 — route-level cost breakdown — medium — 5d — keep (demo ask, straightforward data join)
- PROD-4410 — rollout canary UI for model pinning — medium+ — 8d — keep (high visibility, needs a canary path)
- PROD-4455 — compact trace view for tracing hooks — small — 2d — keep (low risk, visible improvement)
- PROD-4478 — policy-based routing editor (large) — large — 12d — defer (infra deps, high scope)
- PROD-4492 — intake form validation quirks (UX polish) — small — 1d — keep (easy win, demo polish)
- PROD-4520 — cross-tenant dashboard (privacy review required) — medium — 7d — defer (compliance gating)
- PROD-4533 — route-slice bulk-editor (UX research needed) — medium — 6d — park for research sprint
- PROD-4558 — streaming retry semantics (serving infra) — medium — 6d — escalate to eng-architecture

Sprint commitments (finalized):
1) Route-level cost breakdown (PROD-4382) — owner: Jon Park — deliverable: per-route token/cost UI + export CSV. Acceptance: matches ledger sample, unit tests for cost calc, demo-ready.
2) Rollout canary UI (PROD-4410) — owner: Avery Chen — deliverable: canary toggle, traffic slider, behavioral note. Acceptance: toggle persists, fallback path works.
3) Compact trace view (PROD-4455) — owner: Elliot Singh — deliverable: accordion trace list with error highlights. Acceptance: loads under 500ms for 50 traces.
4) Intake form validation fixes (PROD-4492) — owner: Priya Nambiar — deliverable: improved inline error states, keyboard-first UX. Acceptance: 0 JS console errors, validation tests.
5) Canary rollout smoke test and docs — owner: Marisol Rivera — deliverable: playbook for canary + rollback steps. Acceptance: runbook passes dry-run checklist.
6) Accessibility pass on cutlist modal — owner: UX: TBD — deliverable: keyboard/aria improvements. Acceptance: passes basic axe run.

Wireframe / micro-writeups (notes for design/dev pairs):
- Cutlist modal (small): top-level summary, reasons-for-defer section, quick-action buttons (defer, split, claim). Modal should expose linked Jira keys and one-line rationale. Visual: condensed badges for tags + owner.
- Canary UI sketch: inline traffic slider under rollout card; compact preview of percentage + sample user group label; state machine: draft -> active-canary -> promoted/fallback. Needs copy for multi-model behavior.
- Route cost panel: horizontal stacked bar for token types (prompt/resp/embedding), per-1000 unit cost estimate, and an export action. Provide sample mock data to infra for verification.

Acceptance criteria (shared):
- Each committed ticket must have a single PR template linked and at least one unit/integration test.
- UX mocks attached in PR and conformance checked by owner before code review.
- Rollout toggles must include telemetry events (ui.rollout.toggle) with properties: route_id, percentage, user_id.

Dependencies & Risks:
- PROD-4410 depends on a small routing-policy API change; engineering dependency to be gated by Friday 10/09. Risk: if API slips, fallback plan is a non-interactive card.
- Telemetry schema changes for route cost panel require checkout with observability team (SLA for schema deploy is 1 week).
- Accessibility owner unclear — assign after design sync on 10/05.

Cutlist decisions (deferred this sprint):
- Policy-based routing editor (PROD-4478) — defer to Q4 design+infra.
- Cross-tenant dashboard (PROD-4520) — defer behind compliance signoff.
- Route-slice bulk-editor research (PROD-4533) — park until research slot.

Sprint plan (by day-block):
- Mon 10/07: kickoff, assign owners, design quick sync for canary and modal (2h), infra gating check.
- Tue-Wed 10/08-10/09: implement intake fixes + compact trace view; dev reviews.
- Thu 10/10: stitch route cost panel backend + sample data; QA smoke.
- Fri 10/11: cutlist modal dev + accessibility start; docs smoke for canary playbook.
- Week 2 10/14-10/16: finish canary UI, telemetry hooks, run canary smoke tests; feature freeze 10/16.
- Stabilization 10/17-10/20: bug fixes, polish, PR merges, demo prep.

Open questions / blockers:
- Who owns accessibility QA? (Assign to design lead in sync)
- Telemetry schema: can observability expedite the route cost fields? (Marisol to escalate)
- Can infra deliver a routing-policy toggle API by 10/09? (Jon to confirm)

Next steps (immediately after doc):
- Owners accept tickets in Jira and add PR templates by EOD 10/05.
- Design to deliver low-fi mocks for canary and modal by 10/08.
- Marisol to schedule 30m grooming with eng-arch for PROD-4558 and routing-policy gating.

Notes to self: keep the cutlist modal minimal — avoid adding research spikes into this sprint's scope. Track deferred items in a labeled backlog lane for Q4 planning.

Revision log:
- 2026-10-03 initial draft (A. Chen)
- 2026-10-05 sprint commitments refined after intake sync
- 2026-10-07 owners finalized and dates adjusted for feature freeze
